Concern 1 (real): mix-blend-mode: screen lifts the video's blacks but not perfectly

Here's the math: mix-blend-mode: screen means result = 1 - (1 - top) × (1 - bottom). Pure black (0,0,0) on top means the bottom shows through unchanged. But the video isn't pure black — it's MP4 compression. Compression adds noise. The "black" pixels are actually #020101, #010302, etc., near-black but not zero.

What this means: the brain page won't be cleanly hidden behind the video — there'll be a faint ghost of the brain page visible everywhere, not just through the hole. Especially noticeable on a paper-white background (which the brain page has).

Mitigation options:

CSS contrast filter on the video to push near-blacks down to true zero: filter: contrast(1.1)

Compression-aware threshold: use a CSS color matrix filter to clamp anything under some luminance to black

Better source video: re-encode the MP4 with a higher bitrate so the blacks stay closer to true black

Probably not a blocker, but worth knowing it'll need a small filter tweak.

"Chromatic" ≠ "RGB-split chromatic aberration." Chromatic just means colorful. There's a whole vocabulary of cursor-reactive grid treatments that have nothing to do with prism splits.

Real directions, each with a different feel:

Iridescent / oil-on-water — dots shimmer with shifting holographic colors (pink-purple-teal-gold), like a soap bubble or CD surface. The hue cycles based on position + time. Cursor adds a localized hot spot of saturation. Feel: dreamy, organic, unique.

Thermal / heat-map — cursor leaves a glowing trail behind it. Dots near recent cursor positions are hot (white-yellow-orange-red gradient), fading to cool (blue-violet-black) over a few seconds. Feel: alive, physical, scientific.

Magnetic field lines — dots aren't independent — they're nodes in a field. Cursor acts like a magnet, deforming the grid (dots stretch toward cursor, connecting lines bow). Color tints based on field intensity. Feel: physics-y, controlled, sophisticated.

Watercolor bloom — cursor leaves soft ink-bloom blobs of pigment that diffuse outward and fade. Dots in the bloom area pick up its color and slowly desaturate. Feel: hand-made, painterly, slow.

Liquid mercury — dots near cursor literally flow toward it like quicksilver, then settle back. Color shifts through metallic gradients (silver → gold → copper → chrome). Feel: tactile, surprising, premium.

Constellation / star-map — dots are stars. Cursor proximity makes nearby stars brighten, connect to neighbors with thin glowing lines that pulse. Distant stars stay dim. Feel: cosmic, contemplative.

Vinyl record groove / wave — cursor pushes through the grid like a needle on vinyl, creating concentric rings that propagate outward and fade. Color modulates with ring distance. Feel: rhythmic, audio-inspired.

Stained glass / mosaic light — the entire grid is a stained-glass pane. Cursor position acts as a light source behind it, illuminating different colored regions with varying brightness as it moves. Feel: architectural, layered.

These are real directions, not "design-system-flavored" hedges. Each one has a distinct emotional read. Each one would take a different implementation approach.

Iridescent (1) and liquid mercury (5) are the most "expensive" looking

Thermal (2) and constellation (6) are most "alive"

Watercolor bloom (4) is the most "artistic" in the traditional fine-art sense

Magnetic field (3) is the most "technical" and matches "I am also an engineer"
